title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000032: the 20/20 mutation acceptance gate was self-certifying - it accepted any finding of the expected severity on the scenario's affected artifact, so 8 of 20 scenarios passed on standing defects and 4 declared a detector that did not exist, was unreachable, or could not fire on the record the scenario targets

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Initial record. The mutation acceptance gate matched findings on severity and category after filtering to the scenario's affected artifact ids. Both criteria are shared across rules and an artifact can carry several unrelated defects, so a standing defect inherited from the corpus satisfied scenarios whose own detector did not exist, was unreachable, or read a field the record did not carry. The state was discovered by clearing the corpus's nine standing validator findings, which dropped validate to 0 findings and made the gate's real state visible as 8 of 20 scenarios failing.

evidence: The defect is in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py, in the scenario harness. _apply_mutation_and_detect re-ran _validate_links and _validate_semantic_rules on the mutated corpus, then kept every finding whose artifact_id was in the scenario's affected_ids (or whose description mentioned one). cmd_scenario_test then accepted the scenario if ANY of those findings had expected_finding.severity, or had expected_finding.category. Neither the expected description nor expected_detector was consulted at all, and no finding carried an identity for the rule that produced it. The four detectors were proven absent or unreachable by reading the tool: (1) MUT-013 declares 'Requirement applicability validator'; searching corpus.py for an applicability check finds only coverage-plan rendering and variant-applicability output, and no rule reads a non-applicability marking. (2) MUT-003 declares the revision-consistency rule, which lived only inside _validate_artifact, a method _apply_mutation_and_detect never calls. (3) MUT-006 declares the FTTI budget rule, which read d.get('ftti_ms') or d.get('ftti'); the affected record FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 carries neither - it has fault_tolerant_time_interval_ms and timing_budget.total_ftti_ms, while the rule looked for a third spelling. (4) MUT-009 declares the ASIL validator, which fired only on ABSENCE of asil_justification; an unjustified downgrade leaves the justification present and contradicting the assignment, so the rule could only ever have passed on a corpus that had no justification at all. Two patches did not inject the defect they declared. MUT-019 repointed a link to 'FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 refines FB2-SAF-HAZ-000001'; no hazard is ever the source of a refines link, so that edge terminates immediately and the graph stayed acyclic. MUT-020 deleted FB2-LNK-SAF-000014, one of four verifies links covering FB2-SAF-FSR-000002; the other three (FB2-LNK-SAF-000022, FB2-LNK-SAF-000043, FB2-LNK-SAF-000050) remained. The copy-paste that let a standing finding satisfy an expectation is visible in the fixtures: MUT-003, 006, 008, 009, 010, 017, 019 and 020 all carried expected_finding.description 'safety requirement has no verifies/validates link', a string that describes MUT-020's defect and not their own. That text is the message of the verification_traceability_checker rule, so any finding of that rule on the same artifact satisfied eight scenarios. The true state was measured, not estimated. Before the repair, with validate reporting 0 findings, corpus.py check reported 'Acceptance suite: FAILED' with 7/8 gates and 8 failing scenarios: SCN-MUT-003, 006, 009, 010, 013, 017, 019, 020. After the repair, the same command reports 'Acceptance suite: PASSED' with 10/10 gate lines and 23/23 scenario lines, and every mutation line names the rule that fired.
impact: The claim carried by docs/artifacts/reports/final-acceptance-report.md - '20/20 mutation scenarios detect their injected defect' - was false at the time it was written, and was false before any defect in this corpus was repaired. It was the only evidence the acceptance suite offered that the detectors were live rather than dormant, so the whole negative-testing claim rested on it. Concretely: four scenarios asserted the existence of detection that no code implemented, so a rule could be deleted, renamed or broken and the suite would still have reported 20/20. MUT-009's rule was satisfiable only by an unhealthy corpus, so the suite was reporting the corpus's health under  the guise of testing it. MUT-019 and MUT-020 mutated a corpus and detected nothing their scenario declared, which means two of the twenty data points said nothing about detection at all. And because the harness could not distinguish a detection from a coincidence, a future genuine regression that removed a working detector would have been masked by whatever unrelated defect the affected artifact happened to carry - the failure mode is silent in both directions. For the corpus itself the practical effect was smaller: the eight standing findings that had been satisfying the scenarios were real defects, and they were found and corrected by a separate pass. The harm was to the evidence, not to the records - a measurement that could not fail was being cited as a measurement.
root_cause: The harness had no way to know which rule produced a finding, so it could only ask a weaker question - did anything go wrong here - and then treat the answer as the stronger one - did the specific thing this scenario tests go wrong. Findings were plain dicts of severity, category, artifact_id and description. There was no stable rule identifier, so the expected_detector field that every scenario has always carried was decorative. Two design decisions compounded it. First, filtering findings down to the scenario's affected_ids was intended to scope the check, but scoping by artifact id is not scoping by cause: an artifact carries every defect it has, and the harness could not tell which of them the mutation introduced. Second, there was no baseline. The harness never computed what the detectors said about the unmutated corpus, so it had no way to subtract a pre-existing finding, and a detector that fired on the clean corpus was indistinguishable from one that fired because of the mutation. The harness's own author had noticed the symptom and recorded it as a property rather than as a defect: reports/scenario-validation-report.md stated that 'SCN-MUT-008 is the detector that currently fires on the baseline ... the detector fires on the clean baseline by construction', and treated 20/20 as evidence the detectors were live. A detector firing on the clean corpus is exactly what makes a broken scenario pass, so the observation was correct and its interpretation inverted. The mutations were also never executed against a corpus whose standing findings were cleared, so the property was never observed end to end.
resolution:
RESOLVED, and the vocabulary member is corrected from 'accepted' to 'resolved'. Re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z: acceptance gate [5/8] reports 20/20 mutations passing, each against its OWN declared detector, plus 3/3 change lifecycles, and coverage dimension negative_scenario_validation reports the same 20/20 from the same single scenario execution, so the two cannot disagree.

The mechanism that made that number mean something is intact. Findings carry a stable rule identifier; a scenario is resolved to its declared detector by that identifier, read from the evaluator-only oracle manifest; the detector must be emitted by a rule in this module, checked against the module's own AST so an absent detector fails loudly; the detector must be silent on the unmutated corpus, so a standing defect cannot satisfy it; and the baseline is computed once per run and subtracted. Severity and category are reported and a mismatch is flagged as a fixture defect, but they no longer decide a verdict. Two self-tests pin the anti-self-certification property directly: 'scenario fails when its own detector is disabled' and 'standing finding cannot satisfy a scenario'.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. This resolution does not assert that the mutation suite is complete, that the detector set is correct, or that the 20 scenarios are a sufficient sample of what the corpus could get wrong. It asserts that each of the twenty ran, and that each was detected by the rule it names, on a baseline where that rule was silent. That is a narrower claim than 'the corpus is correct' and it is the claim the evidence supports. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.
validator_finding_verbatim: Not a standing validator finding. The corpus validator reported nothing about this: the harness was green while it was broken. The defect was found by clearing the nine standing validator findings, which dropped validate to 0 findings and exposed the gate's real state, and is recorded here as finding FB2-REV-FND-000032.

reverification.method: docs/artifacts/tests/audit_findings.py - the asserted condition was re-derived from the live corpus (link registries, canonical records, validator source, and the SIL harness's own archived sweep), not read from this record.
reverification.evidence: the asserted condition is a gate that accepts any finding of the expected severity on the scenario's affected artifact. Measured in corpus.py: _match_scenario_finding resolves the scenario to a rule identifier, checks the rule is emitted (yes), and subtracts the unmutated baseline before accepting. `check` reports 20/20 mutations passing against their own declared detectors.
